note: Independent-in-method qualification of the Gate 0C.3 evidence other than the 71 per-defect records: the 150-item index, the two OPL challenges, the three public exposures, the per-capita relationship, the carbon evidence and the retention scheduler search. Statuses use SOURCE_VERIFIED, PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, INFERENCE_ONLY and REQUIRES_RUNTIME_PROOF only.

review.limitation: The reviewer belongs to the same engineering-agent family that prepared the Gate 0C.3 registers. The review re-reads the source with a separate extractor and shares no code with the Gate 0C.3 builder, so it is independent in method. It is not an authority-independent approval and it accepts, ratifies and authorizes nothing.
method: Route wrappers and role floors are re-extracted from each route file by a separate extractor that does not read any Gate 0C.3 register.
Each cited quotation is searched in its cited file.
Each affected operation is looked up in the classified inventory and in its route file.
Each proposed disposition is tested against the rubric precondition the Gate 0C.3 register itself states.
Each absence claim is searched for a contradicting token in the cited source.
The 150-item index is rebuilt from the frozen registers and compared.
notDone: No test, database, browser, deployment or role-title check was run.
No disposition, severity, owner or decision was changed.
No authority-independent reviewer has accepted any record.

deduplication.method: The sets are rebuilt from the frozen defect register (release dispositions and the release-blocking flag), the review queue and the handoff register. The Gate 0C.3 debt index is read only to compare.
deduplication.limitation: This verifies that the index counts each frozen record once. It does not verify that the frozen records are complete: a defect never recorded in the register cannot appear in either count.

reviewRequiredProposals.namedMissingEvidence: The frozen record does not state which organization_members columns the member-floor read returns, so the over-disclosure cannot be graded; roster visibility among members is an outstanding institutional decision.

The frozen record does not establish whether the list query fails on the absent status column or returns rows, so what an unauthenticated caller receives is unknown; it also does not state whether any stored row is unpublished.
A scheduler may exist outside the repository; the frozen record cannot establish whether any invocation runs in the released configuration, so the retention breach cannot be graded.

An executed proof that a caller of one organization receives no row of another organization from the route in the intended release configuration, including the case of the flag unset and the flag at 0.

challenges.limitation: Row-level-security enforcement for the connecting database role and the deployed flag value cannot be read from the repository.

exposures.finding: Each of the three handlers is a plain exported function with no authentication wrapper, so the handler itself does not restrict the caller. None of the three paths is in the proxy allowlist the proxy consults (only /api/docs/openapi.json is), so whether an unauthenticated caller reaches them is decided by the proxy and the deployment, which the repository cannot show. The record keeps the exposure contract as release blocking and does not rely on either reading.
exposures.limitation: The proxy matcher and the deployment edge are not executed here.

perCapita.finding: The health-and-welfare path and the four tax paths are separate advertised paths over the same table at the same member read floor. The source shows the same exposure on both. The difference between the MEDIUM and the HIGH rating is therefore not explained by the route source.
perCapita.carriedGap: The MEDIUM record is not an item of the 150-item index although the route it describes exposes the same ledger at the same floor as the indexed HIGH record. It is cross-referenced here and remains an obligation of its engineering owner; it is not added to the index by this gate.

carbon.method: The files that name carbon accounting are listed from the repository, each is read for an estimate or measurement statement, and the four route files are read for an import of any carbon component.
carbon.supersededStatement: No table, service, persona source, register entry or product caller names carbon accounting or Azure emissions monitoring.
carbon.narrowerSupportedFinding: Sources outside the four route files do name carbon accounting. None of them has been demonstrated to supply measured evidence to the four classified routes: no route file imports a carbon component, and the components record their figures as estimates or caller-entered amounts.
notEstablished: That no measured carbon data source exists anywhere in the platform.
That the backend recording path is outside the released scope.
That a source citation is absent from every register for the four operations.
carbon.limitation: Absence of an import in the four files shows no source-level link. It does not show that the components are unused at runtime or that no measured feed exists in a deployment.

limitations: No test, database, browser, deployment, role-title or scheduler check was run.
A source reading shows what the repository declares. It does not show what a deployment enforces.
The reviewer is method-independent only and is not an authority-independent approver.
